fact_check_log.claim: Intro: Australia has no marriage licence to apply for; you give a NOIM to an authorised celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding
Intro: you marry before that celebrant and 2 witnesses
Intro (as drafted): the registry 'registers the marriage'
Intro (after edit 1): celebrant submits the paperwork to the state or territory registry within 14 days
Takeaway 1: no licence; NOIM to authorised celebrant 1 to 18 months before
Takeaway 2: licence permits, certificate records; official copy from the registry counts, not the ceremonial one
Takeaway 2: ceremonial certificate is not the official certificate
Takeaway 3: New Zealand and Hawaii issue licences through their own authorities, each with own timing rules
Takeaway 3: timing rules (NZ 3 working days / 3 months; Hawaii 30 days)
Takeaway 3: Hawaii licence timing
Takeaway 4: decision framing (no factual claim)
Why Australia issues no licence: Marriage Act 1961 and Marriage Regulations 2017 set the rules
Why Australia issues no licence: AGD guidance on getting married does not use the term marriage licence (softened wording per source-pack verify item)
Why Australia issues no licence: the guidance describes giving a NOIM form to an authorised celebrant
NOIM: section 42 requires written notice to the celebrant solemnising the marriage; the NOIM form is that notice
NOIM: at least 1 month and no more than 18 months; can be completed overseas if marrying in Australia
NOIM (cut by edit 3): less than a month, a prescribed authority may approve
NOIM (cut by edit 3): celebrant needs birth, identity and previous-marriage evidence and must meet each party separately in person
Celebrant: you must be married by an authorised marriage celebrant; four types listed by AGD
Celebrant: until Commonwealth-registered, a person cannot accept a NOIM or solemnise a marriage
Words: s46 celebrant (not a minister of a recognised denomination) must say the words in the presence of witnesses; quoted 'union of 2 people' text
Words (as drafted): 'words that include' omits 'or words to that effect'
Words: s45 quoted vow text, 'or words to that effect'
Words: minister of religion may use any form recognised by their religious body
Signing: 3 certificates signed by couple, celebrant and 2 witnesses over 18
Signing: celebrant must submit paperwork to the state or territory registry within 14 days
Compared: Hawaii DOH treats licence (permits) and certificate (shows legal marriage performed) as different documents
Compared: Australia has no licence, so every document is a certificate (inference from fact_08 and fact_04)
Certificates on the day (as drafted): 'Of the 3 certificates signed ... gives you one'
Certificates on the day (after edit 6): celebrant gives a ceremonial certificate on the day
Certificates on the day: commemorative certificate is not the official legal certificate (BDM Victoria)
Official certificate: apply to the registry; celebrant can do it on your behalf
Official certificate (as drafted): 'generally at a cost' (fee reference, cut by edit 7)
Official certificate: NSW and Victorian registry certificate pages (links only, no claim quoted; verified live by SEO 2026-11-26)
Registry copy matters: needed to change name or prove marriage
Registry copy matters: NSW surname update needs official registry certificate; ceremonial not accepted
Registry copy matters: Centrelink does not accept ceremonial certificates for a legal name change
Overseas: Australian-authorised celebrant cannot perform an overseas marriage; it cannot be registered in Australia
NZ: marriage licence confirms it is legal to marry
NZ: visitors can marry without NZ citizenship
NZ: arrange at least 3 working days before; expires after 3 months
NZ: overseas couples sign a declaration at a registry office after arriving, separate from the ceremony
NZ: declaration is not the ceremony
NZ: ceremony only at places named on the application; name a back-up
Hawaii: licence from an authorised agent needed to marry lawfully
Hawaii: apply online
Hawaii: appear together in person before an agent no sooner than 30 days before
Hawaii: valid government-issued photo ID each
Hawaii: ceremony within 30 days of pick-up; licence valid only in Hawaii
Hawaii: performer must be licensed by the Department of Health
Hawaii: no state residence or US citizenship requirements
Other destinations: ask the embassy or consulate; CNI or BDM certificates commonly asked; further rules such as residence
Other destinations: DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia; some authorities only accept their own; ask about apostille
Recognition: generally recognised if valid there and would have been valid here
Recognition: valid under local law and Australian law (Smartraveller)
Recognition: you need to have registered the marriage there and hold evidence such as the certificate (NSW BDM)
Recognition: once recognised, cannot marry again in Australia; confirmation of vows or recommitment possible
Recognition: some states and territories do not accept overseas certificates for name change; NSW official change of name; marriage still recognised
Recognition: ask your local registry
Choosing: official certificate after an Australian legal marriage comes from an Australian registry
Choosing: Advisor line (venue, travel, vendors, payments anywhere in the world; single point of contact) from brand-facts 'Claims we can make'; paperwork stays with couple, celebrant and registry
Choosing: NZ and Hawaii marry under destination law
Choosing: some states and territories do not accept an overseas certificate for a name change

FAQ 3: celebrant submits paperwork within 14 days; apply for official certificate or ask celebrant
